The three-way choice is a switch rather than an if/else chain -- VC6 emits its dec/je ladder and pushes each fact id straight into the shared call -- and the duplicated suppression-clear before the early return is VC6 tail duplication, not source: writing it out merges the two argument cleanups into one add esp,0x10 where the original keeps add esp,0xc and pop ecx

Reads the fact array back, then re-applies the consequences that do not survive a save. The four fact checks share one logging block VC6 inlined at each site, so it is written once as an inline helper and the shared wide buffer stays a single local. The TRUE/FALSE selection is two wcscpy calls, not a ternary: the original pushes each string straight into the shared call where a ternary materialises the pointer into a register first. As in SaveFactState the handle's incoming slot doubles as the bytes-read scratch
Releases each record's sub-list, clearing the pointer as it goes, then the record array

Loads NPC.DBS records and, for each whose leading count exceeds one and whose 0x9d flag is clear, a trailing sub-list: a count then that many six-byte elements appended to a freshly created list. The count guard is written as an unsigned > 0 rather than a plain truthiness test, which is the difference between the original's jbe and a je

Resolves availability across three skill bands: ordinary skills against the profession, the magic realms 0x18-0x1b against its magic-level offset, and 0x22-0x28 against the attribute records. All 117 instructions are present in the original's order. Two differences remain. The switch is emitted as a range compare where the canonical uses a byte index table over 0x00-0x1b placed after the body: its first and third groups share an address, so the middle band 0x0a-0x11 and 0x13-0x17 is a real case group returning 1 like the default, but an empty break is dropped by VC6 and an explicit return 1 merges the bands into one range compare 41 bytes larger. And the attribute comparison materialises through sbb eax,eax where the original uses sbb al,al, which also forces a zero-extend into the magic-realm tail

Seeks straight to one MONSTERS.DBS record and strips its four name fields at 0x00, 0x30, 0x60 and 0x90. The assertion names both identifiers: uiMonsterIndex and gXStatus.uiMonstersInDatabase, at Local Code\\GameplayDatabase.cpp line 320, which also places the other loaders in this address range in that unit. A failed seek leaves the handle open where every other failure closes it. The index is copied into a local before use: its own incoming slot serves as the bytes-read scratch, and taking that address forces the parameter to memory, so without the copy VC6 reloads it for the stride multiply instead of holding it in ESI across the body
Guards the free and then leaves the pointer dangling, where its fact and level siblings clear it unguarded. Both halves of that asymmetry are the original's

Frees the level record array and clears the pointer. Its relocation-masked hash is identical to DestroyFactDatabase's: the two differ only in which global they name, and masking removes exactly that. The bodies stay distinct in the image, so verification against the address is what separates them, not the hash
A generic guarded free called from three unrelated subsystems, so it is named for its behaviour rather than for any one database
Allocates the status block's two heap buffers, 0xc310 and 0x830 bytes. Both are cleared only after both allocations succeed, so a failed second allocation leaves the first live and unzeroed
Frees each of the status block's two buffers if present and clears the pointer

Clears one 0x106-byte party slot row, then sets the occupied flag, zeroes the field at 0x75 and sets 0xd0 to 0xff before notifying 0x004E8290. Typing the row let UtilityFunctions read the occupied flag by name instead of by index

Clears a 56-byte status block, calls a member function on the object at 0x00683FD7 and clears two byte flags. The member call is spelled __fastcall: VC6 cannot declare __thiscall on a free function, but __fastcall passes its first argument in ECX, which is the instruction the canonical emits
Resets eight slots through 0x0054B300, then sets the two Targeting.cpp state words to -1

Tears down two objects, the second through vtable slot 0 with a byte flag - the scalar deleting destructor MSVC emits for a virtual destructor. That call is a __thiscall virtual with its argument on the stack, which __fastcall cannot express because it would place the argument in EDX and the canonical never writes EDX, so this body alone is C++. Each global is read into a local first; read directly they are reloaded rather than held in ESI
Shared success stub: BringUpEngine uses it as a gate and the 62-entry frame dispatch table parks it in seventeen slots

Rebuilds the view of the primary DirectDraw surface: 0x00402E60 releases and clears the four views this module owns, 0x00421F20 hands back the primary surface, and 0x004044C0 wraps it in the 0x30-byte descriptor carrying its width, height and depth. The success flag has to be assigned to a bool local before it is returned, as in 0x00402970, or VC6 materializes it through cl and copies it to al. Same size and all 13 instructions; the residual is that the original stores the wrapper to the global before testing it and this schedules the test first

Clears three dwords then reports whether 0x00402E30 succeeded. The result must be assigned to a bool local first: returning the comparison directly widens it to a 32-bit 0/1 through neg/sbb/neg, where assigning to a bool gives the canonical test al,al plus setne al

Clears four dwords and raises a flag. The startup spine calls these bool gates, and that is the key: the function returns the flag it sets, so VC6 materialises the 1 into AL once and uses it for both the store and the return. Written as void it emits mov byte ptr,1 instead - same size, different encoding
Clears two dwords and raises a flag, returning it as Function404BA0 does
Returns the 3DVideo.CFG literal whose absence sends WinMain to respawn 3DSetup.EXE

Fills a stack MEMORYSTATUS and returns dwAvailPhys; the caller shifts right by ten and stores kilobytes. All eight instructions match and the size is right. The only difference is scheduling: the original stores dwLength before pushing the argument, and VC6 emits the store after the push for every formulation tried

The window init sequence: registers the Wizardry8 window class, points module loading at the DLL subdirectory, then runs each bring-up gate in order and abandons the sequence the moment one reports failure. Like the smaller gates it returns the flag it raises at the end. It also settles 0x005B1740's signature - it is called with an argument here, so the shared stub is not nullary
Empty in the shipped build - a single ret - which BringUpEngine still calls

Clears the 0x400-entry pointer table then walks it releasing each entry, which can never see a live one because the clear precedes it; both are in the original. Same size and all 26 instructions, using two cursors and a down-counter as the original does rather than an index. The residual is scheduling: the original hoists the flag cursor above the rep stosd and stores through it before testing the entry, and no ordering of those statements reproduces it

Single-instance guard on class and title both spelled Wizardry 8, then the video configuration gate that spawns 3DSetup.EXE and rechecks, then the message loop that ticks a frame when no message waits and the application is active. Same size and all 136 instructions. The residual is two lea scheduling differences: the original computes the MSG address between two argument pushes where VC6 emits it after the last one

Registered with atexit as BringUpEngine's first act. Guarded twice: a once flag so a second exit does nothing, and a teardown flag so the long release sequence runs at most once; the engine flag BringUpEngine sets on success decides how much applies. Any message left in the buffer is shown before handing off. Same size and all 52 instructions; two are transposed, the teardown flag store and the strlen cursor load, which no statement ordering reproduces

Appends the subdirectory to the working directory and prepends the result to PATH so plug-in DLLs load from the shipped subdirectory. Structure and call sequence agree - _getcwd, the separator test, two appends, GetEnvironmentVariableA and SetEnvironmentVariableA - but every string call is inlined by VC6 and ours expands to 364 bytes against 342. The empty-subdirectory test and the last-character index are the two spots where the original's inlined strlen differs from what strlen(x)==0 and a conditional index produce; both need their original spelling found

Publishes the three values 0x00422AF0 reports, narrowed to their field widths, then allocates a head node and a copy of the caller's; either allocation failing abandons the whole thing and leaks the first. Same size and all 80 instructions. The residual is scheduling: the original hoists the three out-parameter lea instructions above the register pushes where VC6 emits each just before its own push

Built from the vendored SGP sgp.c. It replaces a reconstructed first-party body that was only structurally-strong; recovering retained SGP code from the image rather than adapting its source is what the evidence policy forbids

Local Code\LoadSaveGame.cpp chain writer. Same size and same 56 instructions as the canonical; the only difference is the recurring register-role swap in the entry pair - the canonical loads the head into EDI and copies EDI to ESI while ours loads ESI and copies ESI to EDI. Two reads deliberately go through the head parameter rather than the cursor, which is the original source naming the parameter where it meant the cursor

VC6 SP5 O2 G6 MD body is byte-exact after masking the four call relocations and the two global operands; Local Code\LoadSaveGame.cpp chain reader that rebuilds the sibling links the file only records as present

Walks the Miles 3D providers for the one whose name matches the configured string, opens it and its listener, and records whether the provider exposes EAX environment selection. Any failure leaves the subsystem closed and still reports success, so audio never blocks bring-up. Reaches 351 bytes against 369 with 110 of 118 instructions. Two residuals: the original re-reads the 3D flag before the provider walk where a short-circuited condition reads it once, and the buffer pointer store is scheduled differently

Brings the renderer up, shows the window and, when the INSPECTOR switch was given, loads that extension from the DLL subdirectory before returning to the original working directory. Each gate that fails returns straight out with the callee's own false still in AL. The two SR.DLL methods must be declared __declspec(dllimport): without it VC6 emits five-byte direct calls to the import thunks where the canonical has six-byte indirect calls through the import address table, which is the entire two-byte size difference and the only thing that stood between 142 matching instructions and an exact body

Local Code\LoadSaveGame.cpp save-directory gate. All 115 instructions of the reconstruction match including the four inline string-table initializers and both inlined strlen expansions; the canonical carries two extra instructions, a second lea of the same cursor into EDX used only for the first call and a mov edx,esi refreshing it at the loop bottom, which is VC6 keeping two names for one induction variable across the rotated back edge

Build stamp and database init. Instruction-identical to the original through the version string, the three formatter calls and the archive open; the whole residual is where VC6 puts the cdecl argument cleanup. The original batches three cleanups into one add esp,0x24 covering the formatter calls and Function412870; this pops after each, 25 add-esp against 22, which is 9 of the 13 bytes. Not reachable from source: chaining the strcat calls grows the frame to 0x4c, and a single-exit goto collapses 292 instructions to 255. /Z7 and /GX were both tested off and change nothing here

Builds the default key binding table: a head node carrying the count 0xfc and a 0x1f8-byte array of 252 key codes, neither allocation checked. The codes are transcribed from the canonical encoding rather than by hand. Indexed writes are wrong - VC6 folds 252 of them into 269 instructions against the original's 517 - so the original writes through a post-incrementing cursor, one mov and one add per entry. That gets the shape but not the encoding: VC6 pairs each store with a +2 displacement and bumps afterwards, six bytes per entry where the original stores at the cursor and then bumps, five. 2268 bytes against 2048, entirely from that one byte

Local Code\LoadSaveGame.cpp monster-group reader; its own assertion at line 1517 names the record. Same 337 bytes and same 125 instructions as the canonical. The residual is the recurring register-role swap where the chunk pointer is read back: the canonical loads it into EDI and copies EDI to ECX for the thiscall while ours loads ECX and copies ECX to EDI, which also slides the trailing stosb of the record clear one slot. The record size is read into the incoming parameter's own stack slot, the SaveFactState dead-slot idiom; a separate local costs four bytes of frame and the canonical opens with a one-byte push

VC6 SP5 O2 G6 MD body is byte-exact after masking the four call relocations and the seven global operands; Local Code\LoadSaveGame.cpp status-header reader, gating the save on an equality test against the 2.0f version in .rdata and publishing four counts that each fall back to one

Window procedure. Four structural corrections against the decompilation, which the body had never been checked against: WM_SIZE shifts lparam logically rather than arithmetically and its second wparam test is an early return; WM_DESTROY reads the engine flag after claiming the teardown rather than hoisting it; the message parameter is signed, since the switch bound is jg and not ja; and WM_SIZING's top and bottom groups converge on one scaling tail where this carried a copy in each, which is where 48 bytes went. WM_SIZE also precedes WM_DESTROY, because VC6 emits case blocks in source order and the original puts the size block at +113 and the destroy block at +182. Code is now 844 bytes, the same extent as the original, with the jump table starting exactly where the original's does at 0x0040152C; 276 instructions against 279. The residual is prologue register ordering and the high half of the packed size, which VC6 folds to test eax,0xffff0000 however it is written - an in-place shift through a local gives the same mask

Local Code\LoadSaveGame.cpp character reader. 162 of the canonical's 163 instructions match, including both inlined strcpy expansions, the shared sprintf the two path spellings jump into, the 0x1862 record clear and the two-stage length-then-body read. Two residuals, neither semantic: the canonical hoists the lea of the directory buffer above the ternary that picks its literal, and it splits the outgoing-argument cleanup after the failure notice into add esp,8 then add esp,0x18 where VC6 here emits one add esp,0x20. Writing the notice as two statements rather than a nested call does not move it

The per-frame tick WinMain calls when no message waits and the application is active. It drives a screen-state stack: the current descriptor at 0x0068EC78 and the pending one immediately after at 0x0068ED10, both 0x98 bytes, which is the element size Function4E2F40 gives CreateStack. A transition copies pending over current and pushes the displaced state. Each state owns five dwords in the table at 0x00647BC8, of which Function4E2F40 walks slot 0 as an initialiser and this walks three more. Reconstructed from the canonical encoding, no decompilation being available: 373 bytes against 364 with 95 of 99 instructions. The residual is register caching - the original keeps 0 in EBX and -1 in EBP across the whole body and compares against them, where literals do not make VC6 cache them

The shipped body allocates a 0xC8 frame and jumps straight to returning true; the CD check it guards - a sprintf of the insert-CD message and a MessageBoxA - sits unreachable between that jump and its target. That is the shape of a patch, not of compiler output: the jump overwrites the first instruction after the prologue, all three GOG builds carry it identically, the retail image is protected so its addresses do not line up, and the demo has no insert-CD string at all. With no unpatched reference in the corpus the original check cannot be recovered, so this models the shipped behaviour rather than the shipped bytes and will not go exact
Clears the flag 0x005B1740's gate sets; reached by both the window procedure's teardown and the shutdown handler
Clears the flag the 0x004086D0 environment selection leaves set

The counterpart to InitializeItemTables: category names first then the tables, each entry freed before its array, and both arrays re-read after every free because nothing tells VC6 that free leaves them alone

Raises three flags, optionally hands the caller's target to 0x005A9E70, then runs a fixed opening sequence of six calls. The two calls into 0x00482720 and 0x00482740 share one stack cleanup, as consecutive cdecl calls do

Optionally releases the global status block's two buffers, then clears the whole block - which zeroes those pointers as a side effect, since they live inside it - and allocates them again. The block opens with the same W8StatusBuffers pair AllocateStatusBuffers manages on a caller-supplied one, and the buffer sizes match

Reads MONSTERS.DBS whole: the count into gXStatus, then - only when the caller wants them - every record into one allocation handed back through the out-parameter, which is why Function4E2F40 can call it with null just to publish the count. Same size and all 112 instructions; two are transposed, the cursor's initialisation and its advance, which no placement of those statements reproduces

The range sibling of LoadMonsterDatabaseRecord, named by its own assertion at GameplayDatabase.cpp line 378. It seeks to the first record and reads the whole inclusive span in one call, with uiEndIndex's own dead slot as the bytes-read out-parameter and a failed seek leaving the handle open. Reaches 232 bytes against 273. The residual is the length arithmetic: the original computes two record offsets through long lea chains and subtracts them, where (uiEndIndex + 1) * 0x297 - uiStartIndex * 0x297 compiles shorter

The new-game reset. It repeats Function54AF30 status-block cycle inline rather than calling it, clears the item in hand and the carried pool, then grants the starting items. The pool and the id list are both walked by address against the symbol that follows them, not by index

Clears the settings block and writes its defaults. Every address it writes falls inside the 0xa4 bytes it clears first, so the block is modelled as one W8GameSettings rather than a run of separate globals; only offsets are established, so the fields keep positional names. Reaches 359 bytes against 361 with the same 72 instructions. The residual is which constants land in which registers: the original holds 0 in AL and reuses CL for 0x40 and then 0xff, where VC6 assigns them differently. Same class of residual as Function4E3340

Resets one 0x118-byte slot in the block at 0x006836B8. The tier it stores twice comes from the character the slot belongs to: the status block's first buffer is an array of W8Character at the 0x1862 stride, and the field at 0x0b01 - the same one party-member selection thresholds against 0x12 and 0x0f - decides between 1 and 2. Writing that as a ternary compiles branchless where the original branches, and caching the array in a local hoists a load the original repeats; both are fixed. Same size and all 82 instructions now; the residual is an EAX/ECX allocation swap through the index computation and the last countdown call being scheduled before two stores rather than after

Clears the 0x1a0a-byte block at 0x006836B8 that 0x0054AF30 and 0x0054B300 also work through, then builds the unit's two owned objects with operator new. Neither class is identified; only their allocation sizes - 0x6c and 0x24 - and the constructor arguments 300.0f and 0 are recovered, and declaring them as classes of exactly those sizes is what reproduces the new-expression cleanup frame VC6 emits around a constructor that can throw. Empty placeholder classes allocate 1 byte and compile to a body less than half the size

All 86 instructions and 276 bytes of code against 275; the COMDAT reads 316 because it carries the two switch jump tables, which the reviewed size excludes

Blits one video-object frame. Establishes the unit's two tables: an eight-byte slot record with the first-frame index at +0x00 and a signed vertical offset at +0x04, and a 0x3c-byte frame record whose first 0x30 bytes are the path it loads from, then a mode selector at +0x30, a loaded flag at +0x34 and the surface at +0x38. The frame table base is 0x0062C430; reading this body alone suggests 0x0062C460, because the first fields it touches are the mode and the surface, and 0x00549090 is what shows the path in front of them. Arity is eight, settled from the encoding - the highest parameter read is entry+0x20 and both call sites push eight - not from the decompiler, which shows a ninth. The row argument is a short and the vertical offset is added in sixteen bits, and the frame index is recomputed for each of the two frame reads rather than held. 240 bytes against 250 with 80 instructions against 83; the residual is register allocation and whether each table read goes through the held slot pointer or its own scaled address

Marks a rectangle dirty on the current page over the 80x60 grid of eight-pixel cells - 0x50 per row, which is 640/8. Skips a page already marked whole and marks it whole when the rectangle covers all of 640x480. Three types came from the encoding, not the decompiler: the page index is a dword rather than the byte its array-subscript use suggests, the cell flags are a byte stored with mov byte ptr, and the low clamps test <= 0 where < 1 reads more naturally - the same test, encoded setle against setl. The clamps are conditional expressions because the original is branchless on the low edge and branches on the high one. 359 bytes against 354 with 127 instructions against 129; the residual is register pressure - the original keeps 0x280 in ebx across the clamping where this spills it to a stack slot, and holding the page index in a local does not change that

Vtable slot 0 of the 18-slot widget base. The canonical is one 52-byte function with the complete destructor folded into the deleting one; the port emits two, a 26-byte ??1 and a 30-byte ??_G that calls it. Confirmed against a from-scratch build directory, so it is not a stale object. VC6 folds them only when the destructor is inline in the class body, and making it inline stops ??_G being emitted at all, because nothing in the port constructs the class and an out-of-line virtual is what currently pulls the vtable into this translation unit. Keeps the held-item cursor in step with the screen: installs the item's cursor on the two screens that allow one in hand, restores the default anywhere else and forgets what was held. Same calls in the same order with the same branches; the whole 30-byte difference is cdecl cleanup placement - the original cleans after each call where VC6 here batches all of them into one add esp,0x3c, and the long-form branches follow from that. Writing the calls with explicit temporaries rather than nested does not move it, which is the same result the other bodies with this residual reached

Drops every region to its resting state: releases the three tracked regions that still carry bit 0x200, disables every region set, then keeps only the low two flag bits on every region and reseeds the fourth tracker from the settings word. Both tables were already modelled - W8RegionSet at 0x0c is the stride-3 run and W8Region at 0x1c the stride-7 one - so the strides confirm the existing layouts rather than needing new ones. 236 bytes against 280 with 61 instructions against 71: the original caches the region index but rematerialises the times-seven address after each call, where VC6 here keeps the address itself live in a callee-saved register across all three blocks

Sets the viewport rectangle and rebuilds the camera view plane to match, applying it to both worlds and re-running 0x00450080 when the flag at 0x00652DA4 is set. The four SR entry points are declared to produce exactly the names Wiz8.exe imports - both setViewPlane overloads, the const getViewPlane and srGERD::flush - which meant extending sr.def from 21 declared imports of the 461 the image has. The plane rectangle is four doubles whose third minus first is a width and fourth minus second a height, which is all this body establishes about it. 411 bytes against 405 with 109 instructions against 111; the residual is x87 scheduling around the two differences and where the doubles spill

Loads a frame surface the first time it is drawn: the path comes out of the frame record itself and the mode picks which of two loaders receives it, each through a request whose first field is 0x40 with the path inline after it. A failure does not return - it formats the path and mode into the assertion message. Both nested VideoObjectsInitialized checks are reproduced; collapsing the inner one costs a call and 31 bytes, so it is real rather than a decompiler artifact. The two request path buffers are 104 and 108 bytes, which the frame proves - the original reserves 0xe0 and only those two plus the surface pointer add up to it, where the decompiler shows the second as 96 because that is as much as this body touches. 382 bytes against 435 with 120 instructions against 131; the residual is register allocation, the original saving esi and edi where this saves ebp

Copies the four clip-rectangle globals into the caller's block. Same 40 bytes and all ten instructions; the only difference is that the original loads the destination pointer before the first global where VC6 here loads the global first

Fills a clipped rectangle on one of the managed surfaces through DDBltSurface. The four negative ids name the surfaces the module owns; anything else is looked up in the list at 0x00650DBC, and the clip rectangle comes from 0x00411820. PARTIAL: 299 bytes against 423, 100 instructions against 140, frame 0x84 where the original reserves 0xac. What the stack map shows and the decompilation does not: two rectangle-shaped blocks are written at esp+0x14 and esp+0x24 from the same four registers, a word is cleared at esp+0x38, the clip block sits at esp+0x48, and the effects block is reached by lea from esp+0x3c with TWO stores into it - esp+0x50 from a caller value and esp+0x58 from a zero-extended word at slot+0x02. The slot pointer is confirmed as edi, loaded from the four globals or from the list entry. Making the fill come from slot+0x02 alone is wrong - it drops the caller value and the body shrinks to 292 - so both feed the effects and which one is the fill is unsettled
